result.title: Embedding-Space Fingerprinting of LoRA Fine-Tunes: Recovering the Training-Data Domain from the Model Artifact Alone
result.summary: When a base language model is fine-tuned with Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA), how much of the training data domain leaks into the resulting artifact? This paper studies whether a simple classifier can recover the domain of a fine-tune given only the model artifact (weight deltas, internal activations on a fixed probe set, or generated text) without ever observing the training data. Using one base model (Qwen3.5-0.8B), 36 LoRA fine-tunes are produced over 18 public datasets in five domains (medical, code, mathematics, non-English text, narrative prose), and three feature families are extracted at decreasing levels of access: white-box weights, gray-box activations, and black-box outputs. A leave-one-dataset-out (LODO) protocol, frozen before any result was seen, tests whether the domain of a fine-tune trained on a previously unseen dataset can be identified. The domain is recoverable well above chance (20%) from gray-box activations (61%) and black-box outputs (64%); white-box weight statistics reach 42%. Contrary to the pre-registered hypothesis that signal decays monotonically from weights to activations to outputs, activations and outputs were more informative than the weight-delta statistics. The black-box result holds unchanged (64%) when only generated text is used, without token probabilities. Domain accuracy is also stable when a third run per dataset is trained on an independently drawn data subsample, and black-box predictions are unaffected by the LoRA rank (8-64). All code and per-run feature vectors are released.

AI.brief_summary: 论文用同一基座模型在18个数据集、5个领域上训练36个LoRA微调，并分别提取白盒权重统计、灰盒激活与黑盒生成文本三类特征，在预先固定的留一数据集协议下检验能否仅凭模型产物恢复训练数据所属领域，结果激活（61%）与输出（64%）均高于权重统计（42%）。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「固定probe集激活＋留一数据集」的探针式诊断可供核查，或可迁移为判断VLM内部状态是否保留视觉证据、以及内部表示与输出信息量是否一致的评测设计；但该工作为纯文本微调取证、非推理任务，线索仍需人工验证。
